items.question: What supreme accomplishment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation can be united in one attainment.
This attainment is described as a great accomplishment.
Such accomplishment can make one dear to the yoginīs.
items.inference: Therefore, the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation renders a practitioner dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: Through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation, one may become dear to the yoginīs.

items.question: Which chapter concludes as it emerges in the moon-island context?
premises: A chapter is identified as having emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
That chapter is specified by an ordinal number.
The ordinal given is the ninth.
items.inference: Therefore, the ninth chapter is the one that has emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: What bodily posture is visualized with the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is conceived as surrounded by fire.
The self is positioned in a specific stance.
That stance is standing on one foot.
items.inference: Therefore, the prescribed visualization places the self surrounded by fire while standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize oneself surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the deity regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly.
The speaker refers to the determination of knowledge.
The speaker asks that this determination be made manifest now.
items.inference: Therefore, the deity is asked to reveal the determination of knowledge to the speaker.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me today.

items.question: What comprehensive understanding of the eight octads is sought by the practitioner?

The knowledge is sought in an exhaustive manner.
items.inference: Therefore, the practitioner seeks to know fully and exhaustively the division of the eight octads.
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and completely the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How can the secret place or wheel be quickly accomplished according to Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is identified as a wheel.
The accomplishment of this wheel is in question.
The desired manner of accomplishment is quick.
items.inference: Therefore, the teaching sought concerns how the secret wheel can be quickly accomplished.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how the secret place, the wheel, is quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why does Bhairava commend the goddess for asking about a matter rare even for the gods?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval of the question.
The goddess has asked Bhairava about something.
That subject is difficult for even the gods to obtain.
items.inference: Therefore, the goddess is praised because her question concerns a matter rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great Goddess; you have asked me about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Which bodily loci are assigned to the syllables kṣa and laṃ in this mapping?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the state of the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with another bodily locus.
That locus for laṃ is the forehead.
items.inference: Therefore, kṣa is mapped to the brahmarandhra and laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though translated as a single forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily loci are assigned to the syllables ṣa and śa in this sequence?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed in another bodily locus.

items.inference: Therefore, ṣa is mapped to the throat region and śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What follows after the place-wheels have been declared in this teaching?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
These wheels have an associated meditation.
The listener is instructed to hear that meditation.
items.inference: Therefore, after declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: Therefore, the meditation envisions a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Meditate on a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner abandon after gaining equanimity through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even-minded state.
Certain social customs are contrasted with this state.
The practitioner is instructed to abandon those customs.
items.inference: Therefore, one who becomes even-minded through practice should abandon village customs.
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the customs of village life.

premises: A form of knowledge involving distant hearing is mentioned.
A power involving paralysis of bonds is mentioned.
These are presented as attained results.
items.inference: Therefore, this stage yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of stobham is compressed in this list-like verse.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized as results of this practice?

Transformation is named as another attainment.

items.inference: Therefore, the practice briefly yields immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and likewise transformation.

premises: The practitioner’s mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation.

items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume forms in many ways.

premises: The practitioner is described in a state of anger.
In that state a power of destruction is asserted.

items.inference: Therefore, when angered, the accomplished practitioner can destroy the whole triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angered, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

premises: A third wheel is introduced in sequence.

items.inference: Therefore, the third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles.

premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned.
Seeing from very far away is mentioned.
Both are presented as resulting powers.
items.inference: Therefore, this accomplishment removes signs of aging and grants vision from a great distance.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

premises: The practice is to be performed in solitude.

The practitioner must be intent on meditation.
items.inference: Therefore, solitary, focused meditation enables one to produce manifold forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create forms in many ways.

items.question: What result is assured for one devoted to constant yogic practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice.
Such dedication is presented as effective.
The stated result is immortality.
items.inference: Therefore, one devoted to constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What consequence follows from daily abstention from eating in this practice?
premises: A regimen of daily non-eating is specified.
This regimen leads to a particular end.
That end is described as death by age.
items.inference: Therefore, daily abstention from eating leads to death by age.
uncertainties: The compound vayo-mṛtyuṃ is terse and its precise doctrinal nuance is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food day by day, one will go to death by old age.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: The practice is constant yogic discipline.
The duration specified is two times eight years.
A specific bodily form results from this practice.
items.inference: Therefore, constant yogic practice for sixteen years yields the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What cosmic power arises from continually contemplating a smoky-colored form?
premises: The practitioner continually contemplates a smoky-colored form.
This contemplation produces a specific power.
The power extends to the triple world.
items.inference: Therefore, constant contemplation of a smoky-colored form enables one to shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoky-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
